q1_issues.issue: "fall on day 17 of Year 1" is the calendar-placement idiom stating when the harvest took place, but the query reifies a separate literal fall eventuality with the harvest as its Theme and hangs the date terms on that fall event instead of on the harvest event-noun witness, so the pattern asks about a falling rather than about the harvest's date.

The noun-attached locative "at the Middle Row" is encoded with the event-oblique head Location on the harvest referent, which the same query otherwise treats as an ordinary entity filling a Theme slot; Where a THING is bars Location on an entity and routes containment "at" to the entity-side head.

q2_gaps: the calendar idiom "<event-noun> falls on <date>" — Time's light-verb-over-event-noun rule names only occurred / happened / took place, so nothing in the instruction set decides between dating the event-noun directly and reifying a literal or scalar-change fall event
notes: "Middle Row" correctly gets Name binding (the capitalized run exceeds the bare class word) with no invented kind atom, and (Day 17) / (Year 1) are the right structured granularity terms. The two issues above are the same underlying indecision about whether thread_harvest is an eventuality or an entity.
